subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <tom@shoply.com>
Cc: Aisha Mendez <aisha.m@shoply.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Thanks again for your time today, Tom — really helpful conversation. Below is a short recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned.

TL;DR
- Shoply is exploring a migration off OpenAI/Anthropic to a combination of open and self-hosted models to reduce unit cost and remove single-vendor lock-in.
- Primary workloads: customer support auto-responses, product description generation, and semantic search for catalogs (embeddings).
- Success criteria: parity on quality & latency, <=20% increase in engineering effort, 30-40% lower per-token cost, and no regression on hallucination for transactional prompts.

Pain points we heard
- Cost volatility and price increases from current providers (OpenAI) impacting unit economics.
- Data residency and vendor lock concerns for regulated partners.
- Latency spikes on peak traffic that affect SLAs for chat and support automation.
- Limited ability to control sampling and deterministic outputs for transactional templates.

Current stack & usage (as discussed)
- Frontend: React app calling a backend API (Node) that routes generation/embeddings.
- Currently using OpenAI for generation (davinci/ gpt-4-ish product tiers) and Anthropic for some safety checks.
- Embeddings: OpenAI embeddings used for semantic search, ~2M requests/month.
- Authentication & secrets: AWS Secrets Manager.
- Observability: Datadog traces + internal logging.

Compatibility needs / must-haves
- REST/SDK parity: function-calling or structured output support, streaming responses, and embeddings API.
- Security: VPC/private deployment option for regulated partners; KMS integration.
- Performance: sub-200ms token latency for short-form transactional prompts in production (p50/p95 targets to be validated).
- Cost controls: support for quantized model variants and batching to reduce per-token cost.

Model shortlist (initial)
- Llama 2 / Llama 3 family (quantized variants) — good embeddings/generation tradeoffs.
- Mistral / Mistral-instruct (strong few-shot performance).
- Falcon 40B / 180B (lower-latency inference variants).
- RedPajama / RedPajama-Instruct (open weights, community-tested).
- Open-orchestrated smaller models for edge use-cases.

Risks & unknowns we flagged
- Safety stack parity: Anthropic-style safety checks will require engineering to reproduce or integrate with Redwood safety layers.
- Embedding drift: switching embedding models may require re-indexing and validation of relevance thresholds.
- Cost for dedicated infra vs managed hosted approach—needs TCO model.

Proposed next steps (agreed on call)
1) Redwood to provide: a migration playbook draft (attached) and a short TCO comparison (hosted vs dedicated) by 2027-03-08.
2) Shoply to share: sample prompts & 50 representative embedding queries + current billing cadence (Aisha will share a billing export).
3) Follow-up technical deep-dive with Shoply infra team (1hr) week of 2027-03-15. Suggested attendees: Rishi, Aditya, Shoply infra leads.

Attachments: redwood-migration-playbook.pdf (high-level plan), shoply-questions.xlsx (initial checklist).

If this matches your notes, Tom, confirm and we'll schedule the deep-dive. Happy to loop in our solutions engineer for a live demo of streaming + function-calling parity.
—
